key_insight: Constrained phase-field topology optimization boosts flexoelectric sensor voltage primarily by increasing mechanically induced source charge, with additional gains from reduced capacitance.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports performance-driven design of microscale flexoelectric devices while accounting for manufacturing variations and structural connectivity.
method: Optimize material distribution using a constrained Allen–Cahn phase-field framework and an infinitesimal-deformation continuum model.
Maximize output voltage, with support for capacitance or stored electrostatic energy objectives.
Address manufacturing variations through worst-case geometric realizations and spectral connectivity constraints.
evidence_signal: Numerical studies cover 2D pressure and bending sensors and a 3D thin-film device; nominal voltage reaches approximately 4.8× the initial value for the pressure sensor and 2.5–3.4× for bending sensors.
watch_item: The abstract reports numerical results rather than experimental validation; fabrication-specific feasibility and performance remain to be established.
paper_title: Constrained Allen-Cahn phase-field topology optimization of flexoelectric devices
